metadata.domain: AI Vision Perception / ADAS / Computer Vision

evidence.trl_pathway: Chiplet-Based AI Accelerators (TRL 3) is scheduled to complete in just 1 quarter (2027-Q1 to 2027-Q2), which is wholly unrealistic for a TRL 3 architecture technology; similarly, Event-Based Vision Processing (TRL 4) completing over ~2.25 years to reach deployment readiness is optimistic but more defensible, while Neuromorphic Computing (TRL 2 → market-ready in ~2.75 years) is extremely aggressive. Multiple pathways violate standard TRL maturation norms.
evidence.strategic_fidelity: The declared 기술선도 strategy is partially reflected in low-TRL exploratory picks (Neuromorphic TRL 2, Chiplet TRL 3, Event-Based TRL 4), but the portfolio is heavily weighted toward semiconductor packaging and memory (HBM, Chiplet, Advanced Packaging) which are not natural R&D-heavy exploratory plays for an AI Vision/ADAS company; the inclusion of two high-TRL process technologies (ISO 26262 at TRL 7, Model Compression at TRL 6) at High investment tier also dilutes the leadership posture.
evidence.competitive_awareness: HBM Integration and Advanced Packaging for AI are clearly outside the core AI Vision Perception / ADAS / Computer Vision domain — these are semiconductor foundry and memory vendor competencies where the company has no established advantage; this domain drift significantly weakens competitive positioning. Even Chiplet-Based AI Accelerators is borderline for a perception/CV software-hardware company. Only Event-Based Vision Processing, Neuromorphic Computing, and ISO 26262/Model Compression are domain-coherent.
evidence.market_timing: For 기술선도 strategy, technologies should complete 1-2 years BEFORE the market boom to establish preemption; however, most technologies are timed to hit exactly at the boom (0.0yr error), which is the 시장이익최대 pattern, not leadership preemption. Event-Based Vision Processing and Neuromorphic Computing complete 0.75yr AFTER their boom windows, which is penalized under both strategies. Only 1-2 technologies achieve the early-completion preemption ideal.
evidence.patent_market_convergence: The selection includes technologies with both patent activity (neuromorphic, event-based vision, chiplet) and market signals (HBM, advanced packaging), suggesting some awareness of convergence zones; however, the heavy inclusion of semiconductor infrastructure technologies (HBM, packaging) appears driven more by market hype than by genuine patent-market convergence analysis relevant to the company's domain, making the convergence appear partially coincidental.

strengths: Neuromorphic Computing and Event-Based Vision Processing are genuinely exploratory, low-TRL picks consistent with long-horizon technology leadership ambitions in perception.
Budget is fully utilized with zero overspend, and the dependency chain from Advanced Packaging → Chiplet → HBM shows some structural dependency thinking.
weaknesses: Two critical dependency violations (Chiplet and HBM both start before their S03 prerequisite completes) render those roadmap entries structurally invalid and unexecutable as planned.

HBM Integration and Advanced Packaging for AI represent severe domain drift for an AI Vision/ADAS company, wasting High-tier investment budget in semiconductor manufacturing where the company has no competitive moat.
missing_technologies: 3D Scene Understanding / Occupancy Grid Networks (core CV leadership technology)
Transformer-based Vision Foundation Models for ADAS (patent-active, domain-relevant)
Multi-modal Sensor Fusion (LiDAR+Camera+Radar) — central to ADAS technology leadership
Uncertainty Quantification / Explainable AI for safety-critical perception
investment_issues: All 7 technologies are assigned Tier=High with identical scoring profiles (4/5/4/3/4), indicating no genuine portfolio differentiation or risk-adjusted prioritization.
High-tier investment in HBM Integration and Advanced Packaging for AI misallocates R&D budget to domains where the company cannot build defensible IP or competitive advantage.
Uniform investment tier ignores the significant uncertainty differential between TRL 2 (Neuromorphic) and TRL 7 (ISO 26262) technologies — risk weighting is absent.
timing_issues: Chiplet-Based AI Accelerators (TRL 3) scheduled for only 1-quarter development (Q1→Q2 2027) is impossibly short for an early-stage architecture technology.
Event-Based Vision Processing completes 0.75yr after its market boom (2029-Q1), missing the window entirely.
Neuromorphic Computing completes 0.75yr after its boom (2030-Q1), and TRL 2 → deployment in 2.75 years is unrealistic.
All technologies are timed to arrive AT the boom rather than 1-2 years BEFORE, contradicting the 기술선도 preemption strategy.
